cues.title: 同质量，换形状
cues.caption: 纸张质量不变，揉成团后下落可以更快。
cues.captionEn: Crumpling paper can change its fall without changing its mass.
cues.zh: 拿两张相同的纸，一张保持平展，另一张揉成团。从同一高度同时释放，纸团会更快接近底部。两份纸的质量相同，结果却不同，这已经提醒我们：空气中的下落快慢，不能只看轻重。改变形状，也改变了空气阻力对运动的影响。
cues.en: Take two identical sheets. Keep one flat and crumple the other, then release both from the same height. The paper ball reaches the bottom sooner even though the masses match. This already shows why falling speed in air cannot be judged from mass alone. Shape changes how air resistance affects the motion.

cues.title: 再与橡皮比较
cues.caption: 纸团更接近橡皮的下落，但仍受空气影响。
cues.captionEn: The paper ball falls more like the eraser, while air still matters.
cues.zh: 再把橡皮加入对照。平纸片落得慢，揉成团的纸却更接近橡皮的运动。我们始终保持释放高度和时刻一致。这里的轨迹用固定姿态作近似，真实纸片还会翻滚。把阻力设成零时，三个物体恢复相同的自由落体规律，不能把空气中的差异带进真空结论。
cues.en: Now include an eraser. Flat paper falls slowly, while the crumpled paper moves more like the eraser. Keep the release height and instant unchanged. These paths assume fixed orientations; real paper also flutters. Setting drag to zero returns all three to the same free-fall rule, separating the air comparison from the vacuum limit.

cues.title: 两石捆绑的反证
cues.caption: 同一个组合，原假设却推出更慢和更快两种结论。
cues.captionEn: The same pair receives contradictory slower and faster predictions.
cues.zh: 换一种研究方式：先假设重石必定落得更快。把轻石和重石捆起来，轻石应拖慢重石，所以组合应该更慢。但组合的总质量更大，按原假设又应该更快。同一个组合不能同时满足两个相反的结论。这是逻辑反证，指出假设有问题，不是实际测出了一条下落轨迹。
cues.en: Try reasoning instead. Assume that a heavier stone must fall faster. Tie a light stone to a heavy one. The light stone should slow the heavy one, making the pair slower. Yet the pair is heavier, so the original assumption also predicts a faster fall. The same pair cannot satisfy both. This is a logical contradiction, not a measured trajectory.

cues.title: 把距离读成时间
cues.titleEn: Read a distance as a time
cues.caption: 接尺前的下落距离，可以换算成反应延迟。
cues.captionEn: The distance fallen before the catch gives a delay estimate.
cues.zh: 最后，用一把尺来测时间。尺子从静止释放，手指在看到它运动后才合拢。等待期间落下的距离越大，延迟就越长。镜头跟着尺子，所以手指相对尺面向上移动。接住的位置对应这段下落距离，再用自由落体关系换算时间。屏幕展示的是模拟，不是在测你的真实反应。
cues.en: Finally, use a ruler to measure time. It starts falling from rest; the fingers close after the observer sees it move. A longer delay means a greater falling distance. This view follows the ruler, so the fingers move upward relative to its scale. Read the catch position, then use free fall to infer the delay. The screen is a simulation, not your reaction test.

cues.title: 时间刻度为什么不等距
cues.titleEn: Why the time marks are uneven
cues.caption: 延迟翻倍，下落距离变为四倍。
cues.captionEn: Double the delay and the falling distance becomes four times larger.
cues.zh: 注意尺上的时间刻度。零点一秒对应四点九厘米，零点二秒对应十九点六厘米。时间翻倍，距离变成四倍。因为从静止下落时，距离与时间的平方成正比，所以越靠后的等时间刻度间隔越大。实际接尺还会受预判和起始位置影响，需要统一条件、重复测量。
cues.en: Look at the time scale. One tenth of a second corresponds to four point nine centimetres; two tenths corresponds to nineteen point six. Twice the time gives four times the distance. For release from rest, distance grows with time squared, so equal-time marks spread farther apart. Real ruler catches also require consistent starting positions and repeated measurements.

question.zh: 同样重的纸，为什么揉成团就落得更快？
question.en: Why does crumpling the same paper make it fall faster?

lead.zh: 先只改变形状，再加入橡皮，最后让空气阻力归零。
lead.en: Change shape first, add an eraser, then remove drag from the same model.

principle.zh: 空气中的落速取决于重力和阻力共同作用；忽略阻力、同高同刻从静止释放时，三者遵循同一自由落体规律。
principle.en: Motion in air depends on both gravity and drag. Without drag, all three follow the same free-fall law from the same height and release time.

question.zh: 真空中把纸揉得更紧，仍会更快落地吗？
question.en: In vacuum, would a tighter paper ball still land sooner?

explanation.zh: 不会。这个模型中形状只通过阻力影响运动；阻力为零后，相同初始条件给出相同的下落。
explanation.en: No. Here shape affects motion through drag; with drag removed, identical starting conditions give identical falls.

question.zh: 把轻石和重石绑在一起，会更快还是更慢？
question.en: Would tying a light stone to a heavy one make them faster or slower?

lead.zh: 把“重者必定更快”的假设，分别用于拖慢作用和组合总质量。
lead.en: Apply the heavier-is-faster premise to both the slowing partner and the combined mass.

principle.zh: 同一假设对同一组合推出相反结果，暴露假设的矛盾；逻辑反证本身不是实测的下落轨迹。
principle.en: Opposite predictions for the same pair reveal a contradiction in the premise. This argument is not a measured falling trajectory.

question.zh: 这段反证能直接告诉我们g的数值吗？
question.en: Can this argument determine the numerical value of g?

explanation.zh: 不能。它排除了只凭轻重判断落速的假设；加速度数值仍需要测量与定量模型。
explanation.en: No. It rejects that premise, while the acceleration still needs measurement and a quantitative model.

question.zh: 尺上的距离，怎样变成看不见的反应时间？
question.en: How can a ruler turn distance into reaction time?

lead.zh: 从静止释放，到手指接住；沿同一尺面标出0.1s和0.2s对应的位置。
lead.en: Release from rest, then catch; mark the positions corresponding to0.1s and0.2s on the same ruler.

principle.zh: 下落距离h=gt²/2，所以时间刻度并不等距；时间加倍，距离变为四倍。
principle.en: Since h=gt²/2, time marks are not equally spaced. Doubling time quadruples distance.

question.zh: 接住时下落距离加倍，反应时间也加倍吗？
question.en: Does twice the falling distance mean twice the reaction time?

explanation.zh: 不是。由t=√(2h/g)，时间只变成原来的√2倍；屏幕模型并不实际测量你的反应能力。
explanation.en: No. With t=√(2h/g), time grows by√2. This screen model does not measure your personal response.

translations.慢放，读数为物理时间: Slow motion; readings use physical time
